micro_counts.protocol: One native instructions:u count at zero and five million iterations; same source except loop bound; CPU 2 and identical environment; not a timing distribution

main_code_comparison.protocol: Compare main-executor mnemonic/operand sequences after removing instruction addresses, resolved branch addresses and RIP-relative relocation displacements; retain symbolic target names and offsets

excluded_attribution_experiment.reason: An initial unobserved allocation loop was virtualized, so it did not exercise weak release membership. Its semantically valid timings are retained but are not evidence of weak-sidecar speedup.

protocol.application: Separate first and confirmation windows; each PHP, baseline, candidate, candidate, baseline, PHP. Fresh result-cache directory per run, warm OS caches, fixed CPU 2. Match output, exit, stderr, five files and twenty findings. Report actual analysis phase separately from whole-command user instructions.
protocol.controls: One warmup per binary; all measured valid samples retained. Five seeded shuffled pairs in confirmation; application windows are not pooled. Observed target uses WeakReference create/get and WeakMap to retain observable object identity.
protocol.limits: 6 GiB aggregate, no swap, exclusive benchmark lock; no native ARM64 result. No layout/ABI/JIT change.

tradeoff.authority: Integrating task review under existing user-authorized performance goal; no separate user approval inferred.
tradeoff.accepted_for: Measured 18.57% instruction and 12.16% time reduction in observed weak lifecycle, 2.195 billion fewer application instructions with equivalent memory and exact PHP semantics.
tradeoff.regressions: Independent controls: shared +2.21%, scalar +3.64%, relative self returns +4.64%; PHPStan confirmation time +0.67%. Keep these controls in subsequent checkpoints.
tradeoff.investigation: Main executor has identical normalized 73261 instructions and size, with different link placement; untyped controls execute essentially identical instruction counts. Frontend empty slots grow while branch misses and opcode/instruction cache misses do not. Same executable path preserves slowdown. This supports native layout sensitivity but does not prove its exact microarchitectural cause. No claim of faster PHPStan.
